The matching article is **“Exome sequencing identifies novel ApoB loss-of-function mutations causing hypobetalipoproteinemia in type 1 diabetes,”** *Acta Diabetologica* (2015), **PMID: 25430706**.

In two DCCT participants with type 1 diabetes and hypobetalipoproteinemia, exome sequencing found heterozygous APOB mutations predicted to cause premature stop codons: at amino acid 1333 in participant 1427 and amino acid 3680 in participant 1078. The variants were inherited from a parent, and both participants had very low LDL-C. These findings support APOB loss of function as a plausible cause of hypobetalipoproteinemia in those two cases. However, the evidence summarized in the abstract does not include functional validation or establish causality beyond these individuals.

Yes. A 2015 *Acta Diabetologica* study (PMID: 25430706) used exome sequencing in two DCCT participants with type 1 diabetes and hypobetalipoproteinemia. It identified heterozygous APOB mutations predicted to introduce premature stop codons at amino acids 1333 and 3680. Both participants had very low LDL-C (36 and 28 mg/dL), and each variant was inherited from a parent.

This supports APOB loss of function as a plausible explanation in those two cases. The reported evidence does not include functional validation or establish causality beyond them.

FINAL DECISION: YES
